items.goal: Invalid cancel/ship status transitions in Ordering.API return 409 Conflict with the domain message instead of 500, and a nonexistent order returns 404. Let OrderingDomainException propagate past IdentifiedCommandHandler's catch-all (e.g. `catch (Exception ex) when (ex is not OrderingDomainException)`), catch it in CancelOrderAsync/ShipOrderAsync and return a 409 problem with the exception message, and distinguish not-found (via the handlers or an order lookup) to return 404. Keep the Ok and BadRequest(empty GUID) paths unchanged and keep other failures as 500. Check that CreateOrder and other identified commands still behave sensibly now that domain exceptions propagate.

items.reason: Generated graphify output (cache/ast JSON, graph.json, graph.html, GRAPH_REPORT.md, manifest.json, build state) was committed under src/Ordering.API/graphify-out/. The root .gitignore rules are anchored to the repo-root graphify-out/, so a nested build from a subdirectory (graphify update . run inside src/Ordering.API) escaped them. Repo policy commits only the semantic cache; the rest is rebuilt by `factory graphify-build`.
items.fix: Remove everything under src/Ordering.API/graphify-out/ from the commit (git rm -r --cached src/Ordering.API/graphify-out and delete the directory). Run `graphify update .` only from the repository root, and optionally add a non-anchored `**/graphify-out/*` ignore rule so nested builds cannot be committed again.

items.reason: Order.SetCancelledStatus rejects Paid as well as Shipped; a separate case guards the second branch of the rule.

items.title: Shipping a Submitted order returns 409
items.reason: The ship endpoint has the same 500 mapping defect (OrdersApi ship path); shipping is only allowed from Paid.

items.reason: A distinct non-Paid source status for the ship rule; re-shipping must not be a server error.

subject: test-automation
reason: All 12 cases are implemented at the functional layer against the real API and database, with exact 409 ProblemDetails detail checks, 404/400 statuses, post-state checks and the same-requestid retry. The only deviation is cosmetic: orders are seeded under a random buyer guid and requests use AutoAuthorizeMiddleware's fixed identity instead of alice's bearer token, and the scenario file is unused by these tests.

items.reason: Case preconditions say orders owned by alice with a bearer token for alice. The tests seed a Buyer named alice with a random identity guid, and requests are authenticated by AutoAuthorizeMiddleware with a fixed identity, so the orders are not owned by the authenticated user. This applies to every case that seeds an order. It has no effect on the outcomes because the cancel and ship endpoints do not check ownership.
